paths.description: Public sports-betting home and primary odds-to-betslip surface; represents the main dashboard template.
Live betting listing; represents real-time market content and high-update interaction.
Football event detail; represents a market detail and selection journey.
Forgot-password form; represents account recovery, labels, validation, and error handling.
Responsible-gaming help; represents long-form help/disclosure and user-safety content.

findings.summary: The interface ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to the light capture, while the DOM reports color-scheme: normal and a white html background.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare light and dark support early, then retint surfaces, text, controls, images, and browser chrome with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Motion continues when reduced motion is requested
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe matched reduce but still found a running 3,000 ms highlight animation.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential highlight and auto-advance animation inside prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: State and route changes do not use View Transitions
findings.evidence: The CSS/script probe found no ::view-transition rule or startViewTransition call across the interactive dashboard and detail route.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document View Transitions for betslip and tab state changes, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long pages lose primary navigation context while scrolling
findings.evidence: The 2,680 px home document uses static navigation and the CSS probe found no scroll-state or scroll-position treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Use sticky chrome with a restrained scroll-state treatment so location and key actions remain understandable.

findings.summary: Rich controls rely on custom roles instead of native primitives
findings.evidence: The platform probe found role=listbox, role=button spans, and checkbox divs, but no dialog, popover, or native disclosure primitives.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace ad-hoc dropdown and disclosure controls with native select, details, popover, or dialog as appropriate.

findings.summary: Promotional and application chrome crowds the core betting content
findings.evidence: The desktop first viewport devotes large regions to two nav rows, promotional hero and banner, registration panel, winner feed, mini games, and betslip around the odds content.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or defer low-value promotional panels and reduce persistent framing around the primary odds and betslip task.

findings.summary: The mobile viewport receives a scaled desktop layout
findings.evidence: At a requested 360x800 viewport, layout metrics reported a 1,000 CSS px layout viewport, no viewport meta, and the screenshot shows the entire dense desktop page scaled to unreadable text.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a real responsive layout with a valid viewport declaration, intrinsic sizing, and mobile reflow instead of shrinking a fixed desktop canvas.

findings.summary: Dashboard components do not adapt at component level
findings.evidence: The platform probe found zero container rules and the narrow screenshot preserves desktop sidebars and tables rather than adapting reusable cards and betslip modules.
findings.suggestedFix: Add container-type to reusable regions and use @container rules to recompose market rows, sidebars, and betslip modules.

findings.summary: Key inputs lack visible focus and targets are undersized
findings.evidence: Focused phone and password fields had outline none and no box shadow; several controls measured 32 px high and the checkbox 13x13 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide clear :focus-visible styles and bring interactive target boxes to an accessible touch size without removing native focus.

findings.summary: Invalid recovery input gives no actionable feedback
findings.evidence: After entering a one-digit phone number on Forgot Password and attempting Next, the captured state remained unchanged with no visible validation explanation.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, connect a specific error message to the field, and announce it through an accessible live region.

findings.summary: The primary page loads far outside good performance ranges
findings.evidence: The trace measured LCP 8.54 s and 3.66 s total blocking time; Lighthouse measured LCP 19.4 s, TBT 990 ms, and performance 42.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP element, reduce startup JavaScript, and split or defer non-critical embeds and dashboard work.

findings.summary: Mobile load produces visible layout shift
findings.evidence: The mobile layout observer measured CLS 0.116 with seven shifts, including 0.063 and 0.042 shifts after four seconds; 31 images lacked dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image and dynamic-panel space with width, height, and aspect-ratio, and stabilize late content.

findings.summary: A multi-second startup task blocks the main thread
findings.evidence: The trace found seven long tasks, including a 3,438.86 ms task, with 3,655.35 ms total blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the startup task, split synchronous initialization, schedule lower-priority work, and defer below-fold widgets.

findings.summary: The page ships a heavy, inefficient dependency chain
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 201 requests and 6.66 MB transferred, including 17 stylesheets, 61 scripts, 9 fonts, multiple parser-inserted stylesheets, and large assets without cache headers.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS, subset and modernize fonts, defer embedded products, and add durable caching to fingerprinted assets.

findings.summary: Large amounts of JavaScript are unused on initial load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 1,017 KiB of removable JavaScript, with several bundles between 48% and 75% unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Route-split desktop/mobile and embedded product code, remove duplicate analytics loaders, and load optional features on demand.

findings.summary: Forms, images, and links lack accessible names
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found login and registration fields with no labels or aria-labels, the images audit found 22 missing alt attributes, and Lighthouse found an unnamed logo link.
findings.suggestedFix: Add persistent labels and correct autocomplete, meaningful alt where needed, empty alt for decoration, and accessible names for icon/logo links.

findings.summary: Heading, landmark, and focus structure is weak
findings.evidence: The home page has no h1, starts its sparse headings at h5, has no main landmark, and focused text inputs show no visible outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a logical h1-led hierarchy and main landmark, remove hidden controls from tab order, and preserve visible focus for every control.

findings.summary: Mobile text is rendered at an unreadably small scale
findings.evidence: The 360 px screenshot scales a 1,000 px desktop surface down to 36%, making odds, labels, winner entries, and help text too small to read comfortably.
findings.suggestedFix: Reflow content at narrow widths and use fluid, user-scalable type with comfortable spacing and line lengths.

findings.summary: The mobile viewport disables useful scaling and reflow
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found user-scalable=no or maximum-scale below 5, while the live page had no desktop viewport meta and rendered a fixed 1,000 px layout into 360 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove zoom restrictions, set width=device-width, initial-scale=1, and verify 400% zoom/reflow with appropriately sized targets.

findings.summary: Images omit intrinsic dimensions and modern delivery hints
findings.evidence: All 31 audited images lacked width and height, 22 below-fold images were not lazy-loaded, and 28 used legacy formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic dimensions, lazy-load below-fold images, and deliver responsive modern formats where appropriate.

findings.summary: Deprecated unload handling blocks browser lifecycle optimizations
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found a deprecated unload listener and six BFCache failure reasons, including an unload handler in the main frame.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace unload with pagehide or visibilitychange where needed and remove avoidable BFCache blockers.

findings.summary: The public page is a JavaScript shell for non-JS crawlers
findings.evidence: The discoverability fetch returned HTTP 500 with 0% rendered-word coverage, no raw title or description, and only a JavaScript-required message in crawler view.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render core content and metadata with stable successful responses, then hydrate enhancements on the client.

findings.summary: Security policy and cookie protections are incomplete
findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff and X-Frame-Options are present, but CSP is missing and all 11 observed cookies lacked Secure and used SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a tested CSP and set Secure plus an appropriate Lax, Strict, or narrowly justified None SameSite policy on cookies.

findings.summary: Tracking and third-party collection are extensive by default
findings.evidence: The page contacted 15 third-party origins, including five known tracker domains; 152 third-party requests transferred 6.21 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize default analytics, gate advertising tags on valid consent, batch telemetry, and remove third parties without clear user value.

findings.summary: Permissions and content security policies are incomplete
findings.evidence: Headers include HSTS, nosniff, SAMEORIGIN and strict-origin-when-cross-origin, but omit both Content-Security-Policy and Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrictive CSP with frame-ancestors and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, then monitor violations before enforcement.

findings.summary: Core content disappears without JavaScript
findings.evidence: The crawler/no-JS capture shows only a JavaScript-required notice; raw fetch returned 500 and had 0% coverage of rendered content words.
findings.suggestedFix: Deliver navigation, odds context, responsible-gaming information, and account recovery as functional HTML before enhancing with JavaScript.

findings.summary: The app-like betting experience has no web manifest or offline fallback signal
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no manifest; the non-JS/failure state is only a generic JavaScript-required notice.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a web app manifest and an intentional offline or flaky-network recovery surface for this app-like service.

findings.summary: The origin failure state is a broken shell rather than recovery UI
findings.evidence: The raw document request returned 500 and crawler view exposed no retry, status, or useful fallback beyond enabling JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a resilient server-rendered error state with retry, status link, and preserved navigation when data or script loading fails.

findings.summary: The sign-in form defaults to persistent session retention
findings.evidence: The first viewport shows “Keep me signed in” selected by default next to sign-in, while deposit and registration prompts dominate the surrounding page.
findings.suggestedFix: Make persistent sign-in an explicit unchecked choice and explain the privacy/security implications in plain language.

findings.summary: Account recovery does not explain invalid input
findings.evidence: A one-digit mobile number and Next attempt produced no visible field-level message or recovery instruction.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate only after interaction, explain the required number format, associate the message with the input, and announce it accessibly.

findings.summary: Sign-in inputs explicitly disable browser assistance
findings.evidence: The login phone and password inputs have autocomplete=off and no labels, preventing reliable autofill and password-manager semantics.
findings.suggestedFix: Use tel/username and current-password autocomplete tokens, with persistent labels and suitable inputmode.

findings.summary: Asset delivery wastes bytes and decoding work
findings.evidence: The images audit found 28 legacy-format images, 22 below-fold images without lazy loading, 11 without srcset, and all 31 without intrinsic dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Use responsive AVIF/WebP sources, intrinsic dimensions, and lazy loading for non-critical imagery.

findings.summary: Startup work and network activity are disproportionate
findings.evidence: The load performs 201 requests, 61 scripts, 62 fetch/XHR requests, and a 3.44 s main-thread task before the dashboard settles.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer background panels and telemetry, batch fetches, and initialize only the visible core market surface.

findings.summary: Third-party code and fonts consume most transferred bytes
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 152 requests and 6.21 MB, including 703.9 KB from Tag Manager and about 1.43 MB of fonts overall.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, remove duplicate tag loads, self-host/subset fonts, and defer mini-game and promotional embeds.

findings.summary: Transactional capabilities are not exposed in a structured agent-safe form
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no agent tooling signal and the no-JS representation exposes none of the visible market or account-recovery capability.
findings.suggestedFix: For explicitly supported agent use cases, expose narrow, confirmable tools with clear schemas, authorization, and human confirmation for wagers.

findings.summary: The initial page has a very large memory footprint
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contains 3,123,569 nodes and 125.1 MB self size, including 523,055 native nodes and 464,305 closures, which is high for one dashboard view.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-mount below-fold and embedded products, reduce retained closures, and set memory budgets for initial and long-lived sessions.
